findings.summary: DeepseekRuntime derives from CodexRuntime and overrides no QuotaKeyOf, so it inherits the virtual 'codex' key (ReviewerRuntime.cs:616); a deepseek row with a key and no base URL, resolved to DeepseekRuntime by RuntimeResolution, that ends spent parks the person's Codex sign-in, and its Ok lifts it.
findings.fix: Add `public override string QuotaKeyOf(string model) => string.Empty;` to DeepseekRuntime (no measured quota, so D3's empty-key rule). Failing test first: AfterRoundAsync over one DeepseekRuntime RateLimited(Spent: true) outcome must leave Standing("codex") null and write nothing; today it fails with 'Expected standing to be <null>, but found QuotaCooldownEntry'.

findings.summary: Judged parks an UNDECIDED agy refusal on a guess when the gauge shows a spent bucket with no reset_time, because the SpentWithoutReset arm ignores 'explicitly'; D10 says a cannot-check undecided refusal is not parked.
findings.fix: Make the arm `QuotaReading.SpentWithoutReset spent when explicitly => Estimated(...)` so an undecided case falls to Unreadable and NotParked. Failing test first: an undecided refusal with QUOTA_SAMPLE's gemini-weekly at 0 and reset_time removed must leave Standing("antigravity/gemini") null with a 'could not check' log; today it fails with 'Expected standing to be <null>, but found QuotaCooldownEntry (Source guess)'.

findings.summary: The consultation classifier reads RateLimit.Hopeless(reason) and ignores RateLimited.Spent, so a Claude monthly-spend-limit outcome with Spent true becomes ConsultFailure.RateLimited (Transient, 'wait a few minutes and consult again') instead of Quota.
findings.fix: Use `(r.Spent ?? RateLimit.Hopeless(r.Reason)) ? new ConsultFailure.Quota(...) : new ConsultFailure.RateLimited(...)`, the same rule as BoundedScheduler.Hopeless. Failing test first: a RateLimited(Spent: true) with the measured spend-limit sentence must classify as ConsultFailure.Quota; today it is ConsultFailure.RateLimited.

findings.summary: The security lane's Refusal answers 'reviewer runtime or credentials unavailable' for any row where canRun is false, so a row parked by a spent quota is excluded with the wrong cause instead of the cooldown sentence the DoD requires.
findings.fix: Pass PanelService.ReasonFor (or a cooldown-sentence func) into SecurityRoster and use it when canRun is false. Failing test first: a security round with a parked codex row must name 'is spent — back at' in its excluded line; today it names 'credentials unavailable'.

findings.summary: Parse reads AGY_ERROR one physical line at a time, so the issue's verbatim pretty-printed refusal ('AGY_ERROR: {' then field lines then '}') yields no error and the refusal stays undecided instead of Spent true.
findings.fix: Parse from the marker to its matching closing brace across lines, or accumulate lines until the JSON parses. Failing test first: exit 3 with the issue's multi-line stderr must give Spent == true; today it gives Spent == null (red: 'Expected verdict.Spent to be True, but found <null>').

findings.summary: Every round with an Ok row produces a Lift decision (line 249) and takes the lock through Mutate even when nothing stands, so an unusable data dir or a busy lock refuses a write that loses nothing and sends a 'spent quota could not be remembered' notice every round.
findings.fix: Drop Lift decisions for keys with no standing entry before Mutate, and skip Mutate when no decision changes the file. Failing test first: a data dir that is a file plus an Ok-only round must not invoke the refused callback; today it does.

findings.summary: ParkedOrNot passes standing.Consecutive + 1 to ReadResetAsync, while D5 says the standing entry's count (0 when none stands), so a guess-parked key refused again gets 60 minutes where the plan's text gives 30.
findings.fix: Either pass standing.Consecutive as D5 literally says (Parked already increments the stored count) or amend D5 and S21 to state the +1. Test first: a standing guess with consecutive 0 plus one refusal must give until = now + 30 min under the literal reading; today it gives 60 min.

findings.summary: The rounds page row still draws the ledger's stated reset (cardResetLine) for a provider whose cooldown stands, so the page can show a reset that disagrees with the card's cooldown line, which D9 says must not happen.
findings.fix: Pass the provider's cooldown into rowLine and draw the cooldown line in place of the ledger hint while one stands. Test first: a rounds block for a cooling provider must show the cooldown time and no ledger reset hint.
